title: Website Analytics Without the Jargon: What to Measure and What to Ignore

cards.heading: Start with questions, not charts
cards.text: Decide what you want to learn before you open a dashboard full of numbers.

cards.heading: Count actions, not just visits
cards.text: Enquiries, bookings and calls usually say more than total traffic does.

cards.heading: Ignore numbers you won't act on
cards.text: If a figure moves and you would change nothing, stop watching it.

cards.heading: Own your analytics account
cards.text: Your business should hold the account, with your developer given access.

cards.heading: Confirm consent in writing
cards.text: Ask what the tool records and whether a consent notice is needed. This is not legal advice.

facebook.message:
Is your website dashboard full of numbers you never act on?
Most small-business sites need only a handful of measures, chosen before launch. Our latest guide explains which numbers help, which can safely be ignored, and what to agree with your developer first, including who owns the account and how consent is handled. Watch for the key points in the short video.

To read the full article, visit the FinTaxTech website and find "Website Analytics Without the Jargon: What to Measure and What to Ignore" in our Blog section.
